research_scope: Exhaustive mathematical-reference identification for six unchanged independent screened formulations; not a review of their mathematical correctness or source licenses.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire independent Stacks-attributed formulation. Its mathematical dependencies are the ambient commutative ring, the ring ideal and the nilpotency of each of its elements; the varying exponent uses the ordinary positive-integer convention. These are not equivalent to nilpotence of the ideal as a whole.

references.context: Commutative algebra
references.matching_note: A commutative-ring ideal is in particular a two-sided ring ideal; the existing generic two-sided-ideal meaning covers this structure.

references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative ring with multiplicative identity
references.matching_note: No independently indexed exact contextual meaning for a commutative unital ring; do not invent a screened definition.

references.context: Commutative algebra: nilpotent element of a commutative ring
references.matching_note: The predicate applies to each element x, not to I as an ideal; distinguish from the existing nilpotent-ideal meaning.

references.phrase: exponent allowed to depend on x
references.disposition: The quantification over a positive integer exponent for each x is treated as ordinary elementary integer quantification, not as a new named mathematical structure.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the entire ideal-nilpotency statement, including its integer exponent and ideal-power notation. Existing meanings support the ambient associative ring and two-sided ideal. Ideal multiplication/powers and the zero ideal are independently needed; a positive integer is an ordinary quantifier, not an assertion that the specific integer-as-equivalence-class construction is required.

references.context: Ring theory
references.matching_note: The underlying two-sided ideal structure is represented; it should not be confused with the multiplication of ideals.

references.context: Ring theory
references.matching_note: The generic associative ring target covers the stated ambient ring without inferring an optional multiplicative identity.

references.context: Ring theory: ideal multiplication and positive integral powers
references.matching_note: Power of an ideal is constructed by ideal multiplication and is not defined by the ring or ideal axioms alone.

references.context: Ring theory: zero ideal of a ring
references.matching_note: The target is the additive-zero ideal of R, not the zero element alone.

references.disposition: Ordinary positive-integer quantification specifies a finite exponent; no source-supported dependency on a particular construction of integers is asserted.

items.review_rationale: Examined the Stacks-attributed radical-ideal characterization and kept it separate from the prime-ideal alternative. Maximal ideal has an existing commutative-unital target, whereas a radical ideal is NOT the same as the Jacobson radical. The commutative-unital ring context and ordinary set intersection/inclusion are recorded explicitly.

references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative ring with multiplicative identity
references.matching_note: The ambient unital commutative-ring convention is not a standalone contextual meaning in the independent catalog.

references.context: Commutative algebra: radical ideal of a commutative ring
references.matching_note: Radical ideal refers to closure under extraction of powers and must not be linked to the different Jacobson-radical meaning.

references.context: Commutative algebra
references.matching_note: The existing maximal-ideal meaning has the required proper-ideal and unital-commutative scope.

references.disposition: Ordinary set intersection of the indicated ideals and ordinary containment I⊆M are treated as set-theoretic operations, not an additional named algebraic definition.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire equivalent prime-ideal formulation independently of its radical-ideal sibling. The quantification is over prime ideals of a commutative ring and their containing maximal ideals. Intersection/containment are elementary set operations; radical ideal does not occur in this formulation and is not an outgoing reference here.

references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative ring with multiplicative identity
references.matching_note: The algebraic commutative-unital ambient ring context requires explicit foundational treatment.

references.context: Commutative algebra
references.matching_note: The stored prime ideal definition has the appropriate commutative-unital scope.

references.context: Commutative algebra
references.matching_note: The existing maximal ideal definition applies to the containing maximal ideals.

references.disposition: Set-theoretic intersection and containment of families of subsets are accepted elementary constructions; no algebraic intersection theorem is asserted.

items.review_rationale: Exhaustively inspected the short principal-ideal-domain formulation. Integral domain and the generic ring-ideal structure are already contextualized; generation of an ideal by a single ring element is a separate missing meaning, not established by the two-sided-ideal definition alone.

references.context: Commutative algebra
references.matching_note: The Stacks-aligned integral domain target explicitly requires a nonzero commutative unital ring.

references.context: Commutative algebra
references.matching_note: Any ideal in an integral domain is two-sided, so the existing ring-ideal meaning is applicable.

references.context: Commutative algebra: principal ideal generated by one element
references.matching_note: The defining principal-ideal construction is required for this characterization and is not yet a standalone meaning.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed both principal-ideal and divisibility formulations under the exact integral-domain context. The two equivalent clauses both depend on the prime ideal and a generated principal ideal; the three divisibility assertions are separately recorded as occurrences of the same missing divisibility notion. The nonunit condition uses the existing unit meaning.

references.matching_note: The nonzero commutative unital domain target is the correct ambient object.

references.matching_note: Nonunit is the negation of ring-unit invertibility in this domain, not an unrelated meaning.
